title: Chapter 44 — The Kitchen & Bath Designer
intro: The channel's highest-leverage relationship — specification power and the partnership machinery.

sections.title: The Specification Power
sections.content:
Kitchen and bath designers have more influence over appliance selection than any other trade professional. They specify the brands, the models, and sometimes the exact SKUs. When a designer says 'use Sub-Zero columns and a Wolf range,' the homeowner almost always follows that recommendation.

This makes the designer the most valuable trade relationship you can build. One active designer who specifies 15 kitchens per year at $8,000-$20,000 in appliances per kitchen is a $120,000-$300,000 annual account.

sections.title: What Designers Need From You
sections.content:
Product knowledge deeper than their own — they need you to be the appliance expert so they can focus on design. Finish and panel-ready options — they need to know every available finish, every custom color, every panel specification. Integration specs — cutout dimensions, panel requirements, handle compatibility, ventilation clearances.

And they need a partner. Not someone who takes orders. Someone who catches mistakes before they cost $5,000 in custom cabinetry rework. Someone who calls and says 'the dishwasher you specified is discontinued — here is the replacement model with the same panel dimensions.'

sections.title: The Partnership Model
sections.content:
Invite designers to your showroom for after-hours product training. Host designer events with food, drinks, and new product previews. Send them spec updates when manufacturers change models. Create a co-branded design board service — you build the appliance layout with specs and pricing, they present it to their client.

Every happy designer knows 3-5 builders. Every designer works with multiple clients per year. One strong designer relationship multiplies across the entire trade channel.
